title: Zhou Dynasty
capsule: The Zhou dynasty, founded c.1046 BC when King Wu of Zhou defeated the Shang at the Battle of Muye, was the longest-ruling dynasty in Chinese history, conventionally divided into Western Zhou (c.1046–771 BC) and Eastern Zhou (770–256 BC). The dataset span of −1000 to −751 covers the Western Zhou period, when the royal court at Hao (near modern Xi'an) exercised genuine suzerainty over a network of feudal lords through the fengjian system, producing the bronze ritual vessels and early texts that defined Chinese classical civilization. Western Zhou collapsed in 771 BC when King You's court was sacked by Quanrong nomads and the Zhou capital shifted east to Luoyi, inaugurating the fractured Spring and Autumn period.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Western Zhou territorial extent is derived primarily from the distribution of bronze vessel inscriptions and archaeological sites of fengjian-granted lords; the core domain is well attested but frontier zones are conjectural.
